neighbours.label: the connective that runs a life span to its end in a biography: 'until' / '—' / 'to' before death, retirement or old age, predicting death; 'until' or 'to' before a clock time or ordinary event stays low
fire: John Hart (born 1790, Leeds—died 1858, York) was an English engraver.
Anna Weiss (born 1822, Vienna—died 1899, Prague) wrote three novels.
The old fisherman lived alone in the cottage until his death in 1907.
She served as the village midwife from girlhood until her death.
He farmed the same hill from youth to old age without a single holiday.
My grandmother kept her diary from childhood until she died at ninety.
The poet stayed in the small coastal town until he died in 1923.
The monk prayed in the abbey every day from boyhood until his death.
quiet: John Hart (Leeds, 1790) published a book of engravings in York.
Anna Weiss moved from Vienna to Prague and wrote three novels.
The old fisherman stayed in the harbour until the tide came in.
She worked as the village midwife from Monday until Thursday.
He farmed the same hill from April to October every single year.
My grandmother kept her diary in a drawer until we found it last week.
The poet stayed in the small coastal town until the end of summer.
The monk prayed in the abbey every day from dawn until breakfast.
